WARNING this game has been compromised and contacts a third party website during play. Also I found using the high seas version solves all of the fps drops and lag spikes. This game is a dumpster fire


Revisiting AGAIN to leave a negative review. The devs have ruined the game performance and lag spikes have been insane for a year now. My PC is literally 150% better than the one I first played on but the performance is worse. Insane.

Im revisiting this game several years later with a negative impression instead of positive. This game has a fantastic first 15 hours with solid gameplay and appealing visuals, but it has nothing for longer engagement. The lack of new maps after all this time is quite astonishing. 

This game has serious scaling issues and all it has to offer is playing the same few maps over and over again. The only good map is the desert map, too. 

However, its the monetization or lack thereof that tips this review positive. This could have been one of the scummiest games ever, and its certainly there in its DNA. However, the game has been perfect in its handling of money, and only offers some optional DLC once in awhile.


Old review:

Gunfire Reborn is built upon an extremely solid core of gameplay, with satisfying guns and enemies that have some personality to them. The visuals are gorgeous and yields high FPS even on a potato. Based simply on the price compared to, say, 10 hours of gameplay, I would have to say its worth it. 

That said, the practical core of the game is a metagame progression loop that is time consuming to say the least. Like most rougelikes\lites you win or mostly lose and gain points to level up a tech tree for the next run. Akin to 90's arcade machines using brutal difficulty to force quick restarts, this game by necessity as an indie title pads out the playtime considerably by using walls of difficulty and a very slow meta progression. While not the worst offender in the genre by any means, I dont appreciate this system. While I am continually unlocking and discovering new content, it comes at a snails pace as he player encounters the same content over and over and over and over again. That said, if the player doesnt mind this system my main objection to the game falls away.

A frequent comment from a quick perusal of reddit\youtube reveals a similar line of thought from the games fanbase...the "true game" requires a lot more play, aka hundreds or thousands of hours invested, before the commentator is able to ''appreciate'' what the game actually is. Any other objection to the games balancing is simply a skill issue and deemed irrelevant. Quite frankly this toxic community attitude, often seen in games such as Dark Souls, fills one with contempt for those games and discourages community interaction.

Balancing is certainly an issue. Fortunately the game leans in favor of the player being OP rather than nerf batting everything, but many weapons are quite useless compared to a somewhat small pool of excellent weapons, and there are some very obvious scroll combinations that if struck upon by chance, will allow the player to proceed much faster and easier through their runs. The games interface and loading screen tips explicitly describe this.

As for content, its alright for the price. Its a cheap game so the standards are way lower than a 60$ title. For the most part you get three map types, with a fourth opening up after what looks to be a substantial grind. Although i have beaten the ship boss once, you need to do so three times? before getting the fourth map which will probably take me a considerable amount of time. You mostly just see the first map over and over again as you try to get a favorable loadout going. There are many varied weapons and sufficient numbers of hem are viable to make it interesting. The enemies and their AI is quite good, as they have some personality and character in the way they move and fight. 

Loot is a bit of an annoyance, honestly. The limitation to two weapons+forcing the use of a basic infinite ammo weapon makes it hard to experiment. Many games I can think of either allow you to hold as many weapon types as there are element types, or one weapon for every ammo type. The games limitation to only 2 is very constraining. There really isnt much in the way of looting since you cant haul your loot back and store it or anything like that. Some kind of base you could build up and go out of missions from could be a great addition in the future.

Speaking of the future, with the current lack of mod support, the game is entirely dependent on the devs pushing out updates. I like the roadmap that pops up ingame and the game will surely continue to grow if they keep pumping out content, and die when they cease to do so. Considering the lack of map variety, this is a dire weakness.

In summary, although I was hemming and hawing between recommending the game or not, I came to the conclusion that this game is a good buy at the price regardless of drawbacks. Furthermore the devs have offered a very fair monetization so far with none of the nonsense plaguing the gaming industry right now, and games that maintain their integrity by avoiding lootboxes deserve some support.
Good game, give it a try yeah?
